doc.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview

chapter: Back to Chicago and the road to jail and illness
title: Don DeFore finds Ware outside Birdland with a Chicago concert plan
summary: A Chicago promoter looks for Ware to bring him to concerts with Griffin, Rollins and Coltrane, and Tommy Potter helps him find him.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: No. The latter part of '59, around November, some guy come out of Chicago -- he's dead now --

you know, a fellow named Don[Defore]-- he come up with the big idea that he'd come to New York -- and he had signed Johnny Griffin and Johnny was back in Chicago then, and he wanted Sonny Rollins, and he's gonna get John Coltrane; each one of wanted them to come and play a concert at the University of Chicago. He was promoting it like that.

So he comes and finds me and says, well, you know how people are -- this particular night, I just happened to hanging out in front of the Birdland, and Tommy Potter was working downstairs with somebody, and like, musicians -- we didn't have dressing rooms. I mean in all those big clubs, you didn't have no place where the musicians could go and sit after you got off the bandstand. You couldn't sit at the tables, as that was for customers. And at the back of the service bar, you had to move out the way because the waiters were coming in and taking orders, and you didn't want to stand by the bar all the time, so you'd come outside; you'd come out on the stage.

That's right. You come out, you know, and that meant the guys would go in some other bar or restaurant or somewhere and watch the clock in order to get back for your next set. So I came upstairs with Tommy Potter and here's this wild looking dude running up and he says, 'Say Tom, do you know where I can find Wilbur Ware?'

He said, 'Man, I got a job for him out of Chicago, and I can't find him.' So Tom looks at me and I look at Tommy, and Tommy said to him 'You know Wilbur Ware?' -- and he says, 'Yeah, man, I'm from Chicago; I know Wilbur. Do you know where I can find him?'

And Tom says, 'But you do know Wilbur, don't you?' and he said, 'Yes, I know him'; and he said, 'Well, what you want with him, man?' and he showed me this placard that he's got with my name all over it and Johnny Griffin and Jody Christian and Phil Thomas on drums, and the next one was gonna be Sonny Rollins with the same rhythm section, and he said, 'Man, if you know where he's at, please tell him' and I said, 'Well, man I am Wilbur Ware.' But all I could do was just laugh, and Tommy said, 'Yeah?' and 'You knew him, huh?' And he said, 'Well, man ... you know how it is.' -- and do you know that I stayed with that cat; that cat would not let me out of his sight. And, you know, that he went down to the Western Union, and he sent off for the money to get the tickets, and he said, 'You're not getting out of my sight; you going back to Chicago.' Just like that.
